Introduction

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) released the National Family Health Survey – 6
(NFHS-6), conducted during 2023-24.
It provides vital data up to the district level on:

   •  Population indicators
   •  Health indicators
   •   Nutrition indicators
   •  Family welfare indicators

NFHS-6 is the sixth in the series, since its launch in the early 1990s, after

   •  NFHS-1 (1992–93)
   •  NFHS-2 (1998–99)
   •  NFHS-3 (2005–06)
   •  NFHS-4 (2015–16)
   •  NFHS-5 (2019–21)

Conducted by: International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai as the nodal agency
Two Phases: NFHS-6 was conducted in two phases

   •  Phase 1: 28th May 2023 to 26th February 2024
   •  Phase 2: 7th February 2024 to 31st December 2024

NFHS-6 Coverage:

   •  6.79 lakh households across 715 districts.
   •  Surveyed 716397 and 100977 men.

New Thematics/Dimensions in NFHS-6

   •  Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Coverage: For the first time, it tracks the reach and impact of welfare
      schemes delivered directly via bank transfers.
   •  Self-Help Group (SHG) Footprints: It maps the expansion and social influence of women-led SHGs
       across rural and urban environments.
   •   Digital Literacy & Financial Independence: It documents the sharp rise in women's digital
        integration, tracking parameters like individual mobile phone usage, independent banking habits,
      and digital financial transactions.

Expanded Biochemical Scope (CAB)

   •   Clinical, Anthropometric, and Biochemical testing protocols were modified, notably integrating
       universal HIV testing into its framework

Key Concerns/Challenges Highlighted by NHFS – 6

   •   Rising non-communicable diseases (NCDs)
   •   Lifestyle-related health risks
   •  Dual burden of undernutrition and rising overweight/obesity among adults

Significance of NFHS-6


The NFHS-6 findings indicate steady progress towards achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
The survey highlights improvements in:

   •  Maternal and child health
   •   Nutrition outcomes
   •  Women’s empowerment
   •  Access to healthcare and financial services
